title: Completed integral twist lines commute with finite scalar base change
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and $S$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $E\subset F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with completed coefficient sheaves $R_E=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,S}$ and $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,S}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $T=\mathbf Z_\ell(1)_S$ be the rank-one twist sheaf of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Use the canonical identifications from the defining formula in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and clause 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], namely $\mathcal O_H(1)\cong T\otimes_{\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,S}}R_H$ for $H=E,F$, with $\mathcal O_H(m)$ formed by tensor powers for $m\geq0$ and sheaf duals [def-pur-sheaf-hom] for $m<0$. Then there are canonical isomorphisms of $R_F$-modules, natural in $S$, $$\mathcal O_E(m)\otimes_{R_E}R_F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_F(m)$$ for every $m\in\mathbf Z$. For $m\geq0$ they are induced by tensor associativity, and for $m<0$ they are induced by the base-change map on sheaf duals; these isomorphisms are compatible with evaluation, tensor powers, and the inclusions in a tower $E\subset F\subset G$.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: integral and common-finite-stage coefficients; canonical scalar base change of the first twist line and its tensor/dual powers in returned item step 9.

proof.text: Put $A=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,S}$ and $L_H=\mathcal O_H(1)$. Clauses 2 and 3 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] give $T$ locally free of rank one over $A$ and $R_H\cong A\otimes_{(\mathbf Z_\ell)_S}(\mathcal O_H)_S$. The defining formula of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] therefore gives $i_H:T\otimes_A R_H\cong L_H$: after the latter substitution its map is $t\otimes(z\otimes a)\mapsto zt\otimes a$, with inverse $t\otimes a\mapsto t\otimes(1\otimes a)$. Both composites are identities by the balanced tensor relations. All maps are sheaf maps, since the sectionwise formulas commute with restriction and hence extend through the sheafification defining tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The inclusion of integer rings induces $R_E\to R_F$ in this presentation, by $z\otimes a\mapsto z\otimes a$ with $a$ mapped to $\mathcal O_F$; it is compatible with towers. This is also the canonical map of the completed coefficient sheaves [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]: composing with each finite quotient gives the inclusion followed by that quotient, which characterizes the map into the inverse limit.

source.place: First sentence (scalar extension of the first twist), and final sentence (integral coefficients); use the existing rank-one and completion comparison, not an interchange of tensor with an arbitrary limit.

proof.text: Through $i_E$ and $i_F$, define $c_1:L_E\otimes_{R_E}R_F\to L_F$ by $(t\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto t\otimes\iota_{EF}(a)b$. Its inverse sends $t\otimes b$ to $(t\otimes1)\otimes b$. The inverse is $A$-balanced because $(zt\otimes1)\otimes b=(t\otimes z)\otimes b=(t\otimes1)\otimes zb$; the other balancing and additivity identities follow from the same tensor relations. The composites send $t\otimes b$ to itself and $(t\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $(t\otimes1)\otimes\iota_{EF}(a)b=(t\otimes a)\otimes b$. Thus they are inverse sheaf morphisms. Their construction is independent of a local generator of $T$.

source.place: First sentence and final sentence: explicit associativity comparison for the first integral twist.

proof.text: For $m=0$ use $c_0:R_E\otimes_{R_E}R_F\cong R_F$, $a\otimes b\mapsto\iota_{EF}(a)b$, with inverse $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. For positive powers, apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] to the identity underlying topos and the ring map $R_E\to R_F$. Its assertion is precisely $(M\otimes_{R_E}N)\otimes_{R_E}R_F\cong(M\otimes_{R_E}R_F)\otimes_{R_F}(N\otimes_{R_E}R_F)$. Starting with $c_1$, induction on $m$ and the recursive tensor-power definition in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] now give $c_m:L_E^{\otimes m}\otimes_{R_E}R_F\cong L_F^{\otimes m}$. In the induction step compose the displayed comparison with $c_m\otimes c_1$; its inverse is the reverse composite of the displayed inverses. These are exactly the positive twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Locally, for a generator $e$ of $T$, the map sends $(a e_E^{\otimes m})\otimes b$ to $\iota_{EF}(a)b e_F^{\otimes m}$, where $e_H=i_H(e\otimes1)$.

source.place: Tensor-power sentence and final sentence: positive integral powers, including their zero-th unit.

proof.text: Fix $n>0$, put $P_H=\mathcal O_H(n)$, and use the sheaf dual $P_H^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{R_H}(P_H,R_H)$ of [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Define $\beta:P_E^\vee\otimes_{R_E}R_F\to(P_E\otimes_{R_E}R_F)^\vee$ on local tensors by $\beta(\varphi\otimes b)(x\otimes c)=\iota_{EF}(\varphi(x))bc$. Linearity of $\varphi$ checks the $R_E$-balancing in $x\otimes c$ and in $\varphi\otimes b$; restriction of sheaf maps checks restriction compatibility. The sheaf tensor definition and sheaf-Hom definition therefore give this map globally. It is equivalently adjoint to scalar extension of evaluation under the closed tensor adjunction [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]. Define $c_{-n}$ as $\beta$ followed by precomposition with $c_n^{-1}:P_F\to P_E\otimes_{R_E}R_F$. By [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] its domain and codomain are exactly $\mathcal O_E(-n)\otimes_{R_E}R_F$ and $\mathcal O_F(-n)$.

source.place: Internal-Hom sentence and final sentence: construction of the negative comparison from evaluation; the map, rather than an unsupported general Hom/base-change isomorphism, is written explicitly.

proof.text: On the cover trivializing $T$ in clause 2 of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], $P_H$ has generator $p_H=e_H^{\otimes n}$. Its dual has generator $p_H^\vee$ characterized by $p_H^\vee(p_H)=1$: on every object over the cover, a linear sheaf map out of the free rank-one sheaf is determined by its value on $p_H$, so evaluation at $p_H$ and $a\mapsto(xp_H\mapsto ax)$ are inverse. The formula of step 4 sends $p_E^\vee\otimes b$ to $b p_F^\vee$. Hence $c_{-n}$ is an isomorphism locally, with inverse $b p_F^\vee\mapsto p_E^\vee\otimes b$. On overlaps these inverses agree, since they are inverses of the same globally defined map: if $u,v$ invert $c_{-n}$, then $u=u c_{-n}v=v$. They glue by the sheaf axiom to its global inverse. This proves every negative case. The same formula gives compatibility with evaluation: the evaluation of $c_{-n}(\varphi\otimes b)$ on $c_n(x\otimes c)$ is $\iota_{EF}(\varphi(x))bc$, exactly scalar extension of evaluation.

source.place: Internal-Hom sentence and final sentence: rank-one verification of the dual comparison and evaluation compatibility.

proof.text: The maps respect tensor powers and the canonical contractions between opposite powers. To check all signs together, on a trivializing cover write $e_H^m$ for the positive tensor generator if $m>0$, the unit if $m=0$, and the dual tensor generator if $m<0$. Tensor associativity and symmetry of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], together with evaluation, identify $e_H^a\otimes e_H^b$ with $e_H^{a+b}$: for opposite signs cancel each paired $e_H$ and $e_H^\vee$ by $e_H^\vee(e_H)=1$. Every $c_m$ sends $(x e_E^m)\otimes y$ to $\iota_{EF}(x)y e_F^m$. Thus the two routes through any tensor-power comparison send $((x e_E^a)\otimes(y e_E^b))\otimes z$ to $\iota_{EF}(xy)z e_F^{a+b}$. These equalities on free generators establish equality of the sheaf maps, and separatedness makes the equalities global. A different local generator $ue$ scales $e_H^m$ by $u^m$ for every integer $m$, so these checks do not depend on the trivialization.

source.place: Tensor-power/internal-Hom sentence: coherence with tensor products and contractions, checked on generators for all signs.

proof.text: For $E\subset F\subset G$, the transitivity identification $((M\otimes_{R_E}R_F)\otimes_{R_F}R_G)\cong M\otimes_{R_E}R_G$ sends $(x\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes\iota_{FG}(b)c$, with inverse $x\otimes c\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes c$. These formulas satisfy the balancing relations and are inverse, as in step 2. On a local twist generator, scalar extension first through $F$ and then through $G$ sends $((a e_E^m)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $\iota_{EG}(a)\iota_{FG}(b)c e_G^m$; direct extension sends it to the same section, for every integer $m$. Equality is global by the sheaf axiom. For an identity coefficient extension the same formula is the tensor-unit map. This proves the tower compatibility without choosing an integral basis for $\mathcal O_F$ over $\mathcal O_E$.

source.place: Final sentence: common finite stages, here the transitivity of integral coefficient inclusions.

proof.text: For a scheme morphism $h:S'\to S$, $\ell$ is invertible on $S'$. [lem-pur-integral-twist-line-inverse-image] gives ring isomorphisms $\alpha_{h,H}:h^{-1}R_{H,S}\cong R_{H,S'}$ and line isomorphisms $\rho_{h,H}:h^{-1}\mathcal O_H(1)_S\cong\mathcal O_H(1)_{S'}$, semilinear over $\alpha_{h,H}$, sending $h^{-1}(t\otimes a)$ to $\tau_h(h^{-1}t)\otimes a$, and (clause 4) commuting with $\iota_{EF}$ and with $j_{EF}:t\otimes a\mapsto t\otimes a$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] to $h$ with $c=\alpha_{h,H}$; since $c$ is invertible, module pullback is $h^{-1}$ with the transported action. Under $i_H$, $c_1$ is the $R_F$-linear extension of $j_{EF}$, so both routes send $h^{-1}((t\otimes a)\otimes b)$ to $\tau_h(h^{-1}t)\otimes\iota_{EF}(\alpha_{h,E}(h^{-1}a))\alpha_{h,F}(h^{-1}b)$; for $c_0$ the square is clause 4 for $\iota_{EF}$. For $m>0$ compare $m$-th powers by the tensor comparison of the cited lemma applied to $\rho_{h,H}$; its naturality in both variables and the recursion of step 3 give the square by induction. For $m=-n$, $\mathcal O_H(n)$ is finite locally free of rank one (steps 1, 3), and the base-change functor of $h$ preserves finite limits and coverings [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. So [lem-pur-ringed-site-finite-free-dual-pullback] with $c=\alpha_{h,H}$ gives the evaluation-induced isomorphism of pulled-back duals, natural in the line; compose with the dual of the inverse of the positive comparison. Under it the pairing of step 4 pulls back to $(\varphi\otimes b,x\otimes c)\mapsto\iota_{EF}(\varphi(x))bc$ on $S'$, the pairing there, and the closed tensor adjunction [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] makes the two dual maps equal. Precomposition with the pulled-back $c_n^{-1}$ matches by the positive case.
